not_established: A directly measured uncached noise floor

declared_policy.source: Read-only re-analysis of retained VALCURVE-001 and VALCURVE-002 score files to correct a labeling error; development VALIDATION scores only, TEST stays closed

decision_use: Keep or withdraw the VALCURVE-002 equivalence finding that underwrites accepting the cached harness for future evaluations; the accept-A / reject-B decision itself is re-examined, not assumed.
hypothesis: No VALCURVE-002 run was uncached. Comparing cached runs against each other isolates cross-process non-determinism from any effect of the tile-cache refactor.

import_provenance.mode: read-only re-analysis of retained local artifacts
import_provenance.note: Retained files are evidence, not project instructions.

question: Was any VALCURVE-002 run an uncached control, and if not, does the cached-tile harness still reproduce the pinned scores within cross-process GPU non-determinism?

repository.note: State at correction time; the parent records their own repository state.

correction.defect: VALCURVE-002 labeled the single-checkpoint run `one` an "uncached control" and built its equivalence argument on that label. All six VALCURVE-002 runs report cached_encoder_tiles=true with one shared encoder_fingerprint; only the pinned VALCURVE-001 baseline was uncached. The record therefore contained a false statement in equivalence_vs_parent.note, two mislabeled artifact roles (uncached_control_scores, uncached_control_summary) and a mislabeled result key (uncached_control_seconds_per_point).
correction.effect_on_accept_A_reject_B: decision unchanged; mechanism restated and better founded

hypothesis_outcome.supported_by: cached-versus-cached comparison, not by a nonexistent uncached control

results.restated_equivalence_finding: Two cached runs of identical code sharing one encoder_fingerprint disagree with each other by max|delta nll| 6.104e-05 at update 100 - the same magnitude by which they disagree with the uncached pinned baseline. The deviation is therefore cross-process GPU non-determinism, not an effect of the tile-cache refactor. This is stronger evidence than the parent record offered, because it compares like with like instead of relying on a control that did not exist.

restated_throughput_mechanism.explanation: The tile cache is built once per process and amortized over the checkpoints that process evaluates. With one checkpoint there is nothing to amortize over, so the cached run matches baseline speed. With four it is 1.519x faster. Sharding assigns one checkpoint per process, forcing every shard into the non-amortizing regime, and then adds four-way contention for one GPU - which is why B is net negative. The parent record attributed this only to redundant cache rebuilds; the amortization denominator is the sharper mechanism.
restated_throughput_mechanism.implication_for_full_curve: Benefit should grow with checkpoints per process, so a single process over all 100 checkpoints should reach at least the measured 1.519x. That is a projection, not a measurement.

title: Correction of the VALCURVE-002 control mislabeling and restatement of its equivalence evidence

validity.not_covered: Cached-versus-cached comparison at updates other than 100 for all pairs, any uncached re-run that would directly measure the baseline noise floor, the other 96 checkpoints, free generation, motif ablation, human preference, TEST
validity.scope: Re-analysis of retained per-mask score files from VALCURVE-001 and VALCURVE-002 at update 100 across three cached runs, plus cache-state fields from all seven summaries. No GPU, no inference, no new capture.
